title: Resolution of the P versus NP problem

concept.text: A proof either that every problem whose solutions can be verified in polynomial time can also be solved in polynomial time (P = NP), or that some cannot (P ≠ NP). Sources given: https://www.claymath.org/millennium-problems/ ; https://world-of-mathematics.com/blog/millennium-problems-overview/.

page.title: Resolution of the P versus NP problem
page.definition: A mathematical proof determines whether P = NP or P ≠ NP. P contains decision problems solvable by a deterministic algorithm in time bounded by a fixed polynomial in input length; NP contains those whose yes answers have polynomial-length certificates checkable deterministically within such a time bound.

goal.need: Route planning and chip layout are among thousands of problems with NP-complete decision versions. A heuristic found a shortest tour through 85,900 cities, but proving it optimal took over 136 CPU years. If P = NP, planners could in principle find exact optima in polynomial time. Practical gains would depend on the algorithm’s running time at the sizes they face. If P ≠ NP, every exact deterministic solver for these NP-complete problems must exceed any fixed polynomial bound in the worst case, even if it solves typical instances quickly.

statements.quote: There is a polynomial-time algorithm for one if and only if there is a polynomial-time algorithm for all.
statements.context: The passage concerns NP-complete decision problems across the sciences.
Stephen Cook’s official description of one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems announced on May 24, 2000.

completion.title: Clay awards its Millennium Prize for a complete P versus NP solution.
completion.criterion: CMI awards the Millennium Prize for a complete proof of P = NP or P ≠ NP under §§4–7 of its rules. The solution must have appeared in a Qualifying Outlet at least two years earlier, gained general acceptance in the global mathematics community, and passed CMI's examination, including examination by its special advisory committee.
completion.set_by: Clay Mathematics Institute, Millennium Prize Description and Rules, §§4–7, adopted on 26 September 2018.
completion.threshold_quote: a Proposed Solution must satisfy examination by CMI.
completion.basis: The rules accept either direction and distinguish community acceptance from CMI's subsequent examination. This supplies an external acceptance test for the mathematical statement in Cook's official description. CMI lists the problem as unsolved.

milestones.title: Every NP decision problem reduces to Boolean satisfiability in polynomial time.
milestones.criterion: Prove that a satisfying truth assignment can be checked in deterministic polynomial time. For every decision problem L in NP, give a deterministic polynomial-time transformation taking each input x to a Boolean formula that has a satisfying assignment exactly when x is a yes instance of L.
milestones.set_by: Complexity-theory community convention: NP-completeness, defined in CMI's official description, Definition 4; Cook's 1971 construction.
milestones.threshold_quote: we will construct a proposition formula A(w) in conjunctive normal form such that A(w) is satisfiable iff M accepts w.

milestones.title: Constant-depth, polynomial-size AND/OR/NOT circuits cannot compute parity.
milestones.criterion: Prove that no Boolean circuit family computes parity on every input with both depth bounded by a constant and gate count bounded by a polynomial in the number of input bits. AND and OR gates may take arbitrarily many inputs, and NOT gates negate one input. Parity is 1 exactly when an odd number of input bits are 1.
milestones.set_by: Complexity-theory community convention: restricted circuit lower bounds; Furst, Saxe and Sipser, Theorem 3.3.
milestones.threshold_quote: Parity cannot be computed by constant-depth, polynomial-size circuits.

milestones.title: Nondeterministic exponential time has no polynomial-size ACC circuit simulation.
milestones.criterion: Prove that some language decidable in nondeterministic time 2^{n^{O(1)}} has no polynomial-size ACC circuit family. A nonuniform family may use a different circuit for each input length n. Its depth is bounded independently of n. It may use NOT gates and unbounded-fan-in AND, OR and MOD_m gates for a fixed integer m > 1. A MOD_m gate outputs 1 exactly when m divides the sum of its inputs.
milestones.set_by: Complexity-theory community convention: circuit-class separation; Williams, Nonuniform ACC Circuit Lower Bounds.
milestones.threshold_quote: NEXP, the class of languages accepted in nondeterministic exponential time, does not have nonuniform ACC circuits of polynomial size.

milestones.title: A complete P versus NP proof survives at least two years of community scrutiny and gains acceptance.
milestones.criterion: A complete proposed solution survives rigorous examination by the global mathematics community for at least two years and achieves general acceptance, as determined by CMI. This satisfies its first evaluation stage, before CMI's own examination.
milestones.set_by: Clay Mathematics Institute, Millennium Prize Description and Rules, §7(a)(i).
milestones.threshold_quote: survive rigorous examination by the global mathematics community for a minimum of two (2) years.

milestones.title: A complete proposed P versus NP proof appears in a qualifying publication.
milestones.criterion: Publish a complete proposed proof of P = NP or P ≠ NP in an outlet qualifying under §6 of Clay’s rules. The ordinary route is a refereed mathematics publication of worldwide repute meeting §6(e). The Board of Directors may approve relaxed conditions on the Scientific Advisory Board’s recommendation under §6(f).
milestones.set_by: Clay Mathematics Institute, Millennium Prize Description and Rules, §§5–6.
milestones.threshold_quote: the Proposed Solution has been published by a Qualifying Outlet

milestones.title: Some language in nondeterministic quasipolynomial time has no polynomial-size EMAJ ∘ ACC⁰ ∘ THR circuits.
milestones.criterion: Prove that some language decidable in nondeterministic time 2^{(log n)^{O(1)}} has no polynomial-size nonuniform circuit family of the following form. The bottom gates test weighted sums of input bits against thresholds. Their outputs feed constant-depth ACC circuits with a fixed modulus. A single output gate accepts exactly when half its inputs are 1.
milestones.set_by: Complexity-theory community convention for circuit lower bounds, as stated by Vyas and Williams.
milestones.threshold_quote: Quasi-NP does not have EMAJ ∘ ACC⁰ ∘ THR circuits of polynomial size

milestones.title: Clay’s special advisory committee examines the proposed proof and reports to the institute.
milestones.criterion: If Clay decides the proposed solution merits detailed consideration, it convenes a committee of at least three members, including at least two experts in the area of the problem. The committee examines the solution and reports to Clay, which may investigate further before deciding on the prize.
milestones.set_by: Clay Mathematics Institute, Millennium Prize Description and Rules, §7(a)(ii)(3–4).
milestones.threshold_quote: The special advisory committee will report within a reasonable time to CMI.

results.finding: For every NP language and each input, Cook constructs one Boolean formula in polynomial time that is satisfiable exactly for yes instances.
results.detail: The proof constructs A(w) before negating it to obtain the DNF tautology query. The intermediate formula A(w) provides the required SAT reduction. The supplied text does not establish the paper’s review status.

results.finding: Every NQL language reduces to Boolean satisfiability in deterministic O(n(log n)^k) time for some fixed k.
results.detail: The proof as written starts with a quasilinear verifier. Extending the construction to an arbitrary NP language would require an additional argument, such as polynomial padding, that the excerpt does not give.
results.quote: MAIN THEOREM 3.1. Sattsfiability is quasilinear complete.

results.finding: Coq verifies polynomial-time assignment checking and reductions from every NP decision problem to SAT, including 3-SAT.
results.detail: The proof uses a call-by-value λ-calculus for the verifier and all reduction functions. The paper cites polynomial-time equivalence with Turing machines and leaves a direct Coq proof of agreement between the two definitions of NP to future work.

results.detail: Theorem 6.11 derives the unconditional lower bound using an ACC tautology algorithm cited by the authors.

goal.need = "Route planning and chip layout are among thousands of problems with NP-complete decision versions. A heuristic found a shortest tour through 85,900 cities, but proving it optimal took over 136 CPU years. If P = NP, planners could in principle find exact optima in polynomial time. Practical gains would depend on the algorithm\u2019s running time at the sizes they face. If P \u2260 NP, every exact deterministic solver for these NP-complete problems must exceed any fixed polynomial bound in the worst case, even if it solves typical instances quickly.". Reason: The enumeration example counts candidate tours, while a measured exact-solver run shows the cost of establishing optimality and gives context for both possible answers.
add statement by Clay Mathematics Institute, 2000: "Problem Statement. Does P = NP?". Reason: Clay’s official problem description states the exact question selected for the prize.

edit m1: criterion = "Prove that a satisfying truth assignment can be checked in deterministic polynomial time. For every decision problem L in NP, give a deterministic polynomial-time transformation taking each input x to a Boolean formula that has a satisfying assignment exactly when x is a yes instance of L.". Reason: The criterion mixes Cook’s published result with the two requirements for proving that satisfiability is NP-complete.

edit m2: title = "Constant-depth, polynomial-size AND/OR/NOT circuits cannot compute parity."; criterion = "Prove that no Boolean circuit family computes parity on every input with both depth bounded by a constant and gate count bounded by a polynomial in the number of input bits. AND and OR gates may take arbitrarily many inputs, and NOT gates negate one input. Parity is 1 exactly when an odd number of input bits are 1.". Reason: The title omits the gate restriction that makes the parity bound true, and the criterion includes the published verdict.

edit m3: criterion = "Prove that some language decidable in nondeterministic time 2^{n^{O(1)}} has no polynomial-size ACC circuit family. A nonuniform family may use a different circuit for each input length n. Its depth is bounded independently of n. It may use NOT gates and unbounded-fan-in AND, OR and MOD_m gates for a fixed integer m > 1. A MOD_m gate outputs 1 exactly when m divides the sum of its inputs.". Reason: The criterion includes Williams’s result and leaves the meaning of a nonuniform circuit family implicit.
